title: Showcase: the walker walks, the arm picks
summary: Walk the quadruped a marked distance for the family. Use the arm to pick up an object and place it down, with the season's numbers on the board.
materials: the quadruped walker from weeks 6 and 7
the arm and gripper from week 5
a marked walking distance and a small object to pick up
tri-fold science fair board or a large sheet of card
the Maker's Log, open to weeks 5 through 7

steps.title: Plan the presentation
steps.body:
Mark a walking lane of a fixed distance, and set the object the arm will pick up at a fixed spot within reach.

Write the season's key numbers on the board: the torque and reach numbers from week 5, and the tipping distances from week 6. Also add the step length, speed and fall results from week 7.

Plan the presentation in this order.

1. Show the arm and explain torque fading with reach, using its own measured numbers.

2. Have the arm pick up the object and place it down.

3. Walk the quadruped the marked distance, live.

4. Show the board's numbers and say what made the gait fall when it did.

Be ready for one question about which build was hardest to get standing or walking at all.

figure.alt: A top-down showcase layout: the presentation board on the left with the season's numbers, an arm station in the middle for the pick-and-place demo with the object marked beside it, and a marked walking lane on the right running from a start point to a finish point, with the family's viewing spot along the bottom.

steps.title: Rehearse both demos
steps.body:
Run the arm's pick-and-place once at demo settings. Walk the quadruped the marked distance once at the gait speed that did not fall in week 7's table.

Practise explaining, in one sentence each, why the arm loses lifting power farther from the shoulder and why a faster gait falls more.
checklist: The board shows the real numbers from weeks 5, 6 and 7
The arm reliably picks up and places the object at demo settings
The walker reliably completes the marked distance at a speed proven not to fall
I can answer one question about which build was hardest

steps.title: Show the family
steps.body:
Gather the family and present in the order rehearsed: the arm's pick and place, then the walker's marked walk, then the board's numbers.

Invite one question and answer it honestly, naming anything either machine still cannot do reliably.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A short recording of the arm's pick-and-place and the walker's marked walk, plus a photo of the board with all the numbers
